title: R’ Ami bar Chama
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as the well-known Rami bar Chama and says he is always called Ami bar Chama in the Jerusalem Talmud. Hyman finds this Ami form also in the Babylonian Talmud, Pesachim 27b and Ketubot 48b.[^1][^2]

notes.text: “This name” is read relative to the headword Ami, not as a claim that the Jerusalem Talmud always writes Rami. The identification with Rami and the force “always” are Hyman’s claims; no exhaustive concordance or authority merge is supplied.

William Davidson Pesachim 27b fully writes Rav Ami bar Chama, whereas Ketubot 48b fully writes Rabbi Ami bar Chama. The heading’s R’ retains the supplied abbreviated title. Hyman’s identification with Rami and his statement “always” are retained as his claims, without an exhaustive concordance or identity merge.
